alignments.note: Coordinating conjunction to the verse-opening And.
Inflected finite verb takes its English subject pronoun as a rule 7/9 helper; head on the lexical verb said, not the subject.
Preposition governing the pronoun realized by unto (rule 36).

Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech, which the ASV marks by punctuation alone; no English word answers to it (rule 43). A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
Negative indefinite carrying the whole English negation as none. The expressed ἐστιν keeps its own is, so this is not rule 41's emptied-negator configuration.

Expressed copula with the supplied expletive subject There riding along as a rule 7 helper; head on is. Alternatively There could be read as added, but the existential frame is what the copula licenses here.
The determiner slot is occupied by the supplied possessive thy, which belongs to the free genitive σου under rule 20, so the article realizes nothing.
Noun to kindred; the case preposition of stays with ἐκ, which is expressed.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive thy (rule 20).
Relative pronoun to the relativizer that.
Passive finite verb with its auxiliary; head on the lexical verb called (rule 9).
The attributive demonstrative τούτῳ occupies the English determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing (rule 38).
Dative noun with the case preposition by. Rule 21 leaves the case preposition on the noun where no article carries a determiner, and rule 15 permits the discontinuity across this.

review_notes: All 16 source and all 17 target IDs partitioned exactly once; t002 is now inside the εἶπαν unit.
ὅτι is recitative and unrepresented per rule 43; expect a reference-comparison disagreement there.
Both articles are unrepresented for distinct reasons: s009 displaced by the genitive σου (rule 20), s014 displaced by the demonstrative (rule 38).
